report:
## Do Masks Reduce COVID-19 Infections at the Population Level?

**Conclusion: Yes, the weight of evidence supports that widespread mask-wearing reduces COVID-19 transmission, though the effect size varies by mask type and study design.**

**Strongest evidence — randomized controlled trials:**
The largest and most rigorous evidence comes from a cluster-randomized controlled trial in Bangladesh involving over 340,000 people across 600 villages (Science, 2021). This study found that community mask promotion increased mask usage and reduced symptomatic seroprevalence by about 9-10% overall, with surgical masks showing stronger effects than cloth masks—reducing symptomatic infections among adults 60+ by more than a third (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9036942/, https://ncrc.jhsph.edu/research/the-impact-of-community-masking-on-covid-19-a-cluster-randomized-trial-in-bangladesh/).

**Observational and modeling evidence:**
A large observational study published in PNAS/PMC found that population-level mask wearing was associated with a mean reduction in SARS-CoV-2 transmission corresponding to roughly a 19% decrease when accounting for mask-wearing prevalence (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9191667/). A JAMA review similarly concluded that "robust available data support the use of face masks in community settings to reduce transmission" (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2811136).

**Contrasting evidence and caveats:**
The Danish DANMASK-19 trial found no statistically significant protective effect for the *wearer* specifically, though it was not designed to measure community-wide transmission effects and had methodological limitations (https://www.thebottomline.org.uk/summaries/danmask-19/). The 2023 Cochrane review also concluded uncertainty from RCT data alone, though Cochrane's editor-in-chief clarified this was widely misinterpreted as "masks don't work" (https://www.cochrane.org/news/statement-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses-review).

**Bottom line:** Individual-level trials show mixed results, but population-level randomized and observational studies—especially the large Bangladesh RCT—provide solid evidence that widespread masking, particularly with surgical masks, meaningfully reduces community transmission.
